result: The word kavāri⟨NOTE:44⟩ in general means a man who is extremely selfish, miserly, performs no sacrifice and leads a contemptible life. In the present ṛk, where akavārim stands, the word kava means a small, despised person, and the compound is kava-ari: a petty enemy. One who is not a kavāri is an akavāri, that is, an enemy of great power; or an abundant number may also be indicated by it. It is an epithet showing Indra's greatness: one who can face such enemies.

- स्वःयवः (*svaḥyavaḥ*)—those who desire the happiness of heaven and the like ⟨NOTE:59⟩

The sūkta beginning चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*) has twelve Ṛks and is Vaiśvāmitra (its seer is Viśvāmitra) and Aindra (its deity is Indra). The Anukramaṇikā says: चर्षणीधृतं द्वादशाद्यांत्यौ तृचौ जागतगायत्राविति (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ dvādaśādyāṃtyau tṛcau jāgatagāyatrāviti*), i.e. the first triplet is in Jagatī, the last triplet in Gāyatrī, and the remaining Ṛks are in Triṣṭubh. The use of the sūkta is Laiṅgika (by the indication of the text). In the ukthya rite (the Kannada reading उक्ते क्रत्वा (*ukte kratvā*) is garbled) ⟨NOTE:60⟩, in the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, after the anurūpa triplet, the first triplet of this sūkta is to be recited. It is stated in the sūtra: चर्षणीधृतमस्तभ्नाद्दामसुर इति तृचौ (*carṣaṇīdhṛtamastabhnāddāmasura iti tṛcau*) (Ā. 6-1). At the Viṣuvat in the niṣkevalya the triplet नृणामु त्वा (*nṛṇāmu tvā*) is used; this is stated in the Viṣuvān section: नृणामु त्वा नृतमं गीर्भिरुक्थैरिति तिस्रः (*nṛṇāmu tvā nṛtamaṃ gīrbhirukthairiti tisraḥ*) ⟨NOTE:61⟩ (Ā. 8-6). In the Bṛhaspatisava also this triplet is used as the nivid in the niṣkevalya; the sūtra says: नृणामु त्वैति मध्यंदिनः (*nṛṇāmu tvaiti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-5). In the Mahāvrata also this triplet is used in the niṣkevalya.
- उक्ष्यं (*ukṣyaṃ*)—the one praised by hymns in the form of ukta ⟨NOTE:62⟩

result: पितुमान् (*pitumān*)—अन्नर्मा (*annarmā*) ⟨NOTE:109⟩. The word पितु (*pitu*) is stated among the names of food (Ni. 3-9). The sacrificers pray to Agni that their path be pleasant and provided with food. The wish of the sacrificers is described thus: may the gods make the herbs grow with sweet waters, and may Agni bring about for the sacrificers increase, so that there is no deficiency of wealth and of abundant food.

That in the animal sacrifice, when the puroḍāśa-sviṣṭakṛt offering is made, this ṛc स्वदस्व हव्या (*svadasva havyā*) ⟨NOTE:111⟩ is to be recited as the yājyā mantra, is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra सदस्व हव्या समिषो दिदीहीति पुरोडाशस्विस्थकृतः (*sadasva havyā samiṣo didīhīti puroḍāśasvisthakṛtaḥ*) (Ā. 3-5). The wishes prayed for are these: may Agni taste the oblations offered by the sacrificers; grant food to the sacrificers; provide bright foods easily; conquer the sacrificers' enemies; be gracious towards the sacrificers; and grant that rites such as the Agnihotra be accomplished without obstacle.
